user.title: Connect CLM
user.description:
Home Assistant connects to the backend. Your browser uses the web app URL to link your account and display CLM. Include http:// or https:// in every address.

Detected Home Assistant URLs: {ha_urls}

data_description.api_origin: The backend address HA can reach, for example http://clm-api:8080 on a shared Docker network. Use the backend service name and container port, or its IP and published port. Do not add /api.
data_description.workspace_origin: Where you open CLM in a browser, for example https://clm.example.com. This opens account approval and the embedded card; it does not register another server. For local-only use, enter your local web URL here.
data_description.workspace_local_origin: Optional browser URL on your home network, for example https://clm.local. Automatic mode tries this address, its IP fallback, then the default URL from each device. With HTTPS HA, this URL must also use HTTPS.
data_description.workspace_local_fallback_origin: A second local web app URL for devices that cannot resolve the local hostname, for example https://192.168.1.20:8443. Use the frontend port. HTTPS requires a certificate your device trusts for this IP. Leave empty if the default URL works everywhere.
data_description.extra_ha_origins: Normally leave empty. HA supplies its internal, external and cloud URLs. Add another full address only if you open this same HA installation there. These are HA addresses, not CLM addresses, and restrict where embedded authorization is accepted.

error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach this backend address. Check the backend container, service name and port from the HA network.
error.no_ha_url: No Home Assistant browser address is available. Configure HA internal/external URLs in network settings, or add a browser URL below.
error.too_many_origins: A maximum of ten Home Assistant browser addresses is supported.
error.backend_changed: To connect to a different CLM server, add a new integration connection.
error.missing_scheme: This address is missing http:// or https://. Include it, for example http://192.168.1.20:8080.
error.invalid_url: Enter a full HTTP or HTTPS address with a valid port, without paths, usernames, query parameters or fragments.
error.unsupported_server: The running CLM backend is too old for this setup. Update and recreate the backend container; a HACS update does not update that server.
error.not_companion_api: This address does not expose the required CLM companion API. Check that it is the backend service and port.
error.server_denied: The backend refused this connection. Check its authentication and network access configuration.
error.server_redirect: This backend address redirects requests. Enter its direct URL and check the proxy configuration.
error.server_error: The backend returned a server error. Check the CLM backend logs.
error.server_rejected: The backend rejected setup. Check that the running backend image is up to date.
error.invalid_server_response: This address did not return a valid CLM API response. Check that it points to the backend, rather than the web app.

abort.already_configured: This CLM server connection already exists. Use Reconfigure to change its browser addresses.
abort.unsupported_version: Update the CLM backend: it must support multiple Home Assistant browser addresses.
abort.reconfigure_successful: CLM addresses updated. Your account links are preserved.

invoke.name: Run CLM binding
invoke.description: Run an approved action using your linked CLM account.

binding.name: Approved binding
binding.description: The ID of a binding approved in the CLM workspace.

list_bindings.name: List approved CLM bindings
list_bindings.description: Return your non-personal approved workflow bindings and expiry times. Turn off Workflows only to include other actions.

workflows_only.name: Workflows only
workflows_only.description: Show bindings that run CLM workflows.

run_workflow.name: Run CLM workflow
run_workflow.description: Run a non-personal CLM workflow using an approved binding and your linked account. For unattended schedules or sensor triggers, use its MQTT trigger.

binding.name: Approved workflow binding
binding.description: Approve Run automation in the CLM workspace, then copy its binding ID from List approved CLM bindings. This is not the workflow ID.

run_automation.name: Run Home Assistant automation
run_automation.description: Run an existing HA automation with its conditions and bounded CLM action bindings. This does not run a CLM workflow.

start_session.name: Start session and open Selkies
start_session.description: Starts a uniquely named preset using the linked account and supplied PIN, then opens its Selkies viewer on the chosen online Windows worker. HA owns the automation and trigger.

config_entry_id.name: CLM connection
config_entry_id.description: Choose the CLM connection installed in Home Assistant.

device.name: CLM device
device.description: Use the exact device name or ID from CLM Devices or List CLM Windows workers. The Windows worker must be online.

pin.name: Personal Mode PIN
pin.description: The linked CLM account PIN, checked for this call only. HA action data and traces may contain it; it is never sent to the worker.

preset_name.name: Preset name
preset_name.description: Exact unique preset name to start. The action opens its Selkies viewer directly on the selected PC.

incognito.name: Incognito window
incognito.description: Open a new private browser window on the selected Windows PC. This does not change CLM Personal Mode.

account_user_id.name: Linked HA account
account_user_id.description: For unattended automations with multiple linked accounts, select the HA user ID whose CLM link to use. Interactive callers always use their own link.

open_selkies.name: Open matching Selkies viewers
open_selkies.description: Opens existing owned Selkies sessions whose name contains the supplied text, using the PIN for this action only. Does not open a CLM window or unlock the HA card.

user.title: Share an entity with CLM
user.description: Lets a linked CLM account use a light, button, sensor or automation without waiting for it to ask. Delete the entry here to take it back.

data_description.entity: Lights and buttons can be controlled; sensors can be read; automations can be run and used as triggers in CLM.
data_description.account: The Home Assistant user whose linked CLM account gets access. It can only use what this user may use.

error.not_permitted: This user is not allowed to use this entity in Home Assistant.
